dashboard.title: Dashboard
dashboard.subtitle: Live DNS statistics
dashboard.stats_disabled: Statistics are switched off in Settings → Privacy. The totals since start still update; the top lists and the graph stay empty, and earlier statistics are not served back.
dashboard.dropped_stats_warning: {{count}} query stats were dropped under load — counters and the live feed may be undercounting.

queries.title: Query Log
queries.subtitle: Recent DNS queries
queries.clear_confirm: This will permanently delete all query log entries, along with every statistic built from them: top lists, the 24-hour graph, per-device counters and the per-tunnel host lists. This cannot be undone.
queries.log_disabled: The query log is switched off in Settings → Privacy. Queries are still answered, just not recorded.
queries.group_repeats_hint: Fold identical queries in a row into one line

clients.title: Clients
clients.subtitle: Top DNS clients — retained history
clients.filter_placeholder: Filter by name, IP or MAC…
clients.stats_disabled: Statistics are switched off in Settings → Privacy. This page is built from per-device counters, so it stays empty. Names and aliases still work.

blocklist.title: Blocklist
blocklist.subtitle: Blacklist and whitelist management
blocklist.full_check_hint: Matched sources and routing are on the Tools page.

lists.title: Subscription Lists
lists.subtitle: Remote blocklist feeds
lists.remove_confirm: Remove subscription list "{{name}}"? This cannot be undone.
lists.allow_hint: Domains on these lists are never blocked — use them to undo false positives from the blocklists above. Refreshed together with blocklists.
lists.allow_remove_confirm: Remove allowlist "{{name}}"? This cannot be undone.

dns.title: Custom DNS Records
dns.subtitle: Local A / AAAA / CNAME overrides. Wildcards supported: *.home.lan

settings.title: Settings
settings.subtitle: Runtime controls and persisted service configuration
settings.restarting: Server is restarting — waiting for it to come back…
settings.live_changes_sub: These values are patched into the running service immediately.
settings.restart_changes: Saved to disk, then the supervisor brings Ferrite back.
settings.restart_changes_sub: Listener and cache sizing changes require the service to restart.
settings.min_ttl_sub: Minimum TTL for responses cached by ferrite (s). 0 = keep exactly as long as the origin said.
settings.max_ttl_sub: Maximum TTL for responses cached by ferrite (s)
settings.client_ttl_sub: Longest TTL handed to devices (s). ferrite holds the cache, so devices stay thin — this bounds how long a device keeps a stale answer after a list, rule or profile change. Never raises a shorter upstream TTL. 0 = devices don't cache.
settings.log_retention_sub: Delete query log entries older than N days; 0 = keep forever
settings.log_max_mb_sub: Also trim the query log once it passes N MB, oldest first; 0 = no size limit
settings.storage_backend_sqlite_sub: SQLite on disk — history survives a restart.
settings.storage_backend_memory_sub: In RAM only — nothing is written to disk, and history is lost on restart.
settings.storage_path_sub: Where the query log is stored. Pick a RAM-backed mount to spend no writes on the disk — at the cost of losing history on reboot.
settings.storage_ram_warning: This location is in RAM: a reboot clears the query log, and without a size cap it grows into the memory the resolver needs.
settings.blocklist_cache_dir_sub: Where the compiled blocklists are kept. Nothing in it is your data — it is rebuilt from the list servers — and it is written on a refresh, not per query.
settings.blocklist_cache_ram_warning: This location is in RAM: no flash writes, but the cache takes RAM that cannot be paged out (roughly the size of the lists), and every list is downloaded again after a reboot.
settings.api_key_set: Currently set — enter new value to replace
settings.access_sub: Credentials and API key used by the web UI and external clients
settings.password_sub: Web UI login password; leave blank to keep current
settings.web_dir_sub: Override web assets path; blank = default
settings.blocking_enabled_sub: Master switch for DNS blocking; allowed DNS and logging keep running
settings.debug_logging_sub: Verbose logs for diagnosing issues. On by default; turn off if too noisy. Applied immediately.
settings.log_ignore_sub: Domains matching these patterns are resolved normally but hidden from the query log
settings.privacy_sub: What ferrite records about the queries it answers. Both switches take effect on Save, without a restart.
settings.log_queries_sub: Keep one record per query — the Queries page and per-device history. Off: nothing about individual lookups is stored. Statistics keep their own aggregate top lists unless you switch those off as well.
settings.keep_stats_sub: Keep top domains, top clients and the 24-hour graph. Off: the dashboard keeps only the totals since start, which carry no domain or device identity. Top lists, the Clients page and per-device stats stop being served too, including what was stored earlier.
settings.record_nothing_sub: With both off ferrite keeps filtering but stores nothing about what was resolved. The restart snapshot also stops keeping cached domains, so a restart begins with a cold cache.
settings.purge_data_sub: Switching recording off only stops new data. This deletes what is already stored — query log, statistics and counters — and vacuums the database.
settings.purge_data_confirm: Delete the entire query log and all statistics? This cannot be undone.
settings.purged_no_vacuum: Stored data deleted, but the database could not be vacuumed — check the free disk space.
settings.purged_vacuum_running: Stored data deleted. The database is still being rebuilt — the disk space will come back shortly.
settings.no_patterns: No patterns — all queries are logged
settings.dns_bind_sub: Address and port for the DNS listener
settings.cache_size_sub: Maximum number of cached DNS entries
settings.dns_dnssec_sub: Set the DO bit and forward signatures. Enforcement needs a validating resolver over DoT/DoH.
settings.dns_strip_ecs_sub: Strip EDNS Client Subnet from upstream queries so the resolver never learns the client's subnet.
settings.blocklist_cache_size_sub: Recent block/allow decisions kept in RAM
settings.api_bind_sub: Address and port for the HTTP API / web UI
settings.upstream_resolvers_sub: Default DNS resolvers used when no local zone route matches
settings.upstream_sub: Replace the full upstream list. Plain DNS is enough for most LAN/router setups.
settings.upstream_egress_help: Send this resolver's queries through the tunnel. Falls back to direct if the tunnel is down.
settings.zone_routing_sub: Route LAN names and reverse-DNS zones to a specific resolver
settings.zones_sub: Docker bridge mode usually needs a LAN reverse-DNS zone routed to the router DNS.
settings.zones_empty: No explicit zones. Ferrite will use the default upstream resolver list.
settings.panel_sub: Built-in DNS shortcut for the Ferrite web UI
settings.panel_enabled_sub: Serve the built-in panel domain as a local A record
settings.panel_domain_sub: Domain answered by Ferrite, usually fe.te
settings.panel_ipv4_sub: Host/LAN IP to return in Docker bridge mode; blank = auto-detect
settings.panel_url_sub: Display URL for logs and copied links; useful when the web UI runs on a non-80 port
settings.current_config_sub: Raw server config, collapsed until needed
settings.updates_sub: Server and web UI release checks
settings.updates_empty: No update check has been run yet.
settings.restart_timeout: Server did not come back after restart. Reload the page to retry.

errors.rate_limited: Too many attempts. Please wait a moment and try again.
errors.password_empty: Password cannot be empty. Disable password login instead.
errors.password_hash_failed: Could not save the new password.
errors.api_key_empty: API key cannot be empty. Clear it instead.
errors.dns_min_ttl_range: Minimum DNS TTL must be between 0 and 86,400 seconds.
errors.dns_max_ttl_range: Maximum DNS TTL must be between 0 and 86,400 seconds.
errors.dns_ttl_order: Minimum DNS TTL cannot be greater than maximum DNS TTL.
errors.blocklist_cache_size: Blocklist cache size must be greater than 0.
errors.upstream_empty: Add at least one upstream DNS server.
errors.invalid_client_bypass: Client filtering bypass must contain only valid IP or MAC addresses.
errors.client_identity_required: Provide either an IP address or a MAC address.
errors.invalid_client_key: Client must be a valid IP address or MAC address.
errors.web_update_incompatible: This web UI update requires a different server version.

tools.title: Tools
tools.subtitle: DNS, filtering and WHOIS lookups plus egress, certificate and TCP probes — run from the server through its own resolvers and tunnels.
tools.egress_check_help: Connect out through a tunnel and report the observed exit IP.
tools.domain_check_help: Check whether a domain would be filtered, why, and where its traffic routes.

tunnels.title: Tunnels
tunnels.subtitle: Route chosen domains through a tunnel or proxy. Matching domains resolve to ferrite, which forwards them through the selected egress.
tunnels.no_egresses: No egresses yet. Add a Direct or SOCKS5 egress to route through.
tunnels.no_rules: No rules. A plain domain (example.com) routes it and all its subdomains; *.example.com routes subdomains only.
tunnels.no_known_devices: No devices seen yet — they appear once they query.
tunnels.evasion_help: Splits the TLS ClientHello across TCP segments so SNI-based DPI can't read the host name. Leave blank to split automatically inside the SNI.
tunnels.wg_hidden_hint: The PrivateKey is shown masked (********). Leave it as-is to keep the stored key, or paste a fresh .conf to replace it.
tunnels.buffer_over: {{buf}} KB across parallel downloads can exceed the egress's shared kernel UDP buffer (~{{max}} KB) — media may stall mid-load. Raise it: sudo sysctl -w net.core.rmem_max={{rec}} (or use a smaller buffer).
tunnels.kernel_backend_hint: Kernel WireGuard — the OS handles buffering, congestion control and crypto (TCP autotuning, multi-core). The Buffer setting is ignored unless the tunnel falls back to the userspace backend.
tunnels.kernel_buffer: Kernel UDP buffer ≈ {{max}} KB (raise net.core.rmem_max for more)
tunnels.general_sub: Master switch and how ferrite advertises itself to matching clients.
tunnels.enabled_sub: Route matching domains through a tunnel; everything else resolves normally.
tunnels.advertise_ipv4_sub: IPv4 that matching domains resolve to. Blank auto-detects this box's address.
tunnels.advertise_ipv6_sub: IPv6 to advertise alongside IPv4. Optional.
tunnels.max_connections_sub: Upper bound on simultaneously tunneled connections.
tunnels.egresses_sub: The tunnels and proxies traffic can be routed through.
tunnels.rules_sub: Which domains route through which egress, and for which devices.
tunnels.fail_closed_hint: Drop traffic when the egress is down.
tunnels.pattern_help: A plain domain matches it and all subdomains; *.example.com matches subdomains only. Fail-closed drops traffic when the egress is down.
tunnels.col_hits_hint: Connections routed by this rule since ferrite started.
tunnels.alert_webhook_sub: URL POSTed a JSON event when an egress stays down for over a minute (and again on recovery). Works with ntfy or any JSON webhook receiver. Blank = off.
tunnels.probe_target_sub: host:port the health probe connects to through each egress to measure latency. Must be reachable through every tunnel (it gates fail-closed). Blank = 1.1.1.1:443.
tunnels.rule_devices_hint: None selected — the rule applies to every device.
tunnels.rule_service_help: Routes all domains of the service ({{count}}). Messengers, game launchers and Spotify also use their own protocols, which a tunnel can't carry, so they aren't listed.
tunnels.rule_service_help_empty: Messengers, game launchers and Spotify also use their own protocols, which a tunnel can't carry, so they aren't listed.

logs.title: Logs
logs.subtitle: Recent server log records (in-memory; newest at the bottom).

profiles.no_devices: No devices seen yet — they appear once they query.
profiles.allowlists_inherit: None selected — all enabled allowlists apply.
profiles.default_deny_hint: Only allowed domains resolve for these devices: manual allows plus the allowlists above. Local network names (PTR, .lan, .local, your zones) keep working.
profiles.default_deny_warn: Nothing is allowed yet — these devices will effectively lose DNS. Add allow entries or an allowlist first.
profiles.page_subtitle: Rules for chosen devices: services to block, lists to apply, what to allow. Devices in no profile follow the network-wide rules.
profiles.empty_help: Every device follows the network-wide rules. Add a profile to give some devices their own: block TikTok and games on a child's tablet, or allow only a short list on a smart TV.
profiles.no_devices_selected: No devices selected — this profile applies to nobody yet.
profiles.schedule_always: Always on. Add a time window to apply this profile only at certain hours.
profiles.schedule_hint: Outside these hours its devices follow the next profile they are in, or the network-wide rules. When several profiles include a device, the first one that is on wins — the arrows set the order.

pause.banner: Filtering is paused — everything resolves for {{time}} more.

backup.title: Backup & restore
backup.sub: The whole configuration as one config.toml — to keep, or to move to another box.
backup.restore_confirm: Restore "{{name}}"? It replaces the whole configuration and restarts ferrite. The current file is kept as config.toml.bak.
backup.secrets_hint: The file holds secrets — the API key, the password hash, WireGuard private keys. Keep it somewhere safe. A restored file brings its own password: log back in with that one.

services.title: Blocked services
services.help: Block a whole service for every device: its sites, apps and media servers. A whitelist entry still exempts a single domain.
services.profiles_hint: To block a service only on some devices, use a profile.

note.telegram: Telegram's apps reach their servers by IP address, so blocking stops the website and t.me links, not the app itself.
note.facebook: Also stops “Sign in with Facebook” and Facebook widgets on other sites.
